releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.8.2
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 12.8.2 fixes a startup crash on Linux ppc64le and `UnknownIssuer` errors on systems without CA certificates. `pnpm run` no longer installs before every script on CI when `autoDedupe` is enabled, and resolution and hoisted installs on macOS are faster.

### Patch Changes

#### Platforms and environments

- Fixed pnpm crashing on startup on Linux ppc64le [#16380](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16380).

- Fixed installs failing with `UnknownIssuer` on Linux systems without CA certificates, such as `node:24-slim`, when `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` is set. The extra certificates now extend the bundled CA roots [#16365](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16365).

- pnpm now creates its store operation locks and other per-user lock files in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` when it points to a directory only the user can write to. Otherwise, pnpm still uses `/tmp` on Linux and macOS. Sandboxes that block writes to `/tmp` can point `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` at a writable directory [#16390](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16390).

- POSIX bin shims and the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` launchers now run inside a Nix build, where the system default path holds none of the utilities they call. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#16377](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16377).

- In a project that pins another pnpm version, pnpm now passes a command with an option it does not know to the pinned version. Before, pnpm rejected the option before switching, so `pnpm install --auto-dedupe` failed with "Unknown option" even though the pinned pnpm supports it [#16353](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16353).

#### Installing and resolving dependencies

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now fails when `Cargo.lock` does not satisfy a dependency requirement in `Cargo.toml`. The error names the crate and the version the lockfile holds [#16355](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16355).

- `pnpm install` returns "Already up to date" again in a workspace with injected workspace dependencies and a shared lockfile. Since 12.7.0 every repeat install in such a workspace ran the full install and copied the injected projects again.

- With `injectWorkspacePackages: true`, a fresh `pnpm install` now records a workspace dependency as `link:` when its injected copy differs from the project only by an optional peer that peer-dependent dedupe merges. It was recorded as a peer-suffixed `file:` copy [#16354](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16354).

- `pnpm dedupe --check` now passes right after `pnpm dedupe` when deduplication merges variants of a package that differ only in their peers. A lockfile key whose peer suffix named a merged variant now names the variant that replaced it [#16356](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16356).

- When `minimumReleaseAge` hides the version that `latest` points to, pnpm now falls back to a prerelease of the same major before a stable version of an older major. A stable version of the same major is still preferred. Before
…(truncated)

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 11.28.3
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 11.28.3 updates `undici` to clear a security advisory, fixes "database disk image is malformed" errors when several pnpm processes share a store, and makes packages, catalogs, projects, and commands named like `constructor` work.

### Patch Changes

#### Installing packages

* pnpm now ships `undici` 7.29.1, so security scans of pnpm no longer report [GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v).

* pnpm no longer fails with "database disk image is malformed" or reads stale store entries while another pnpm process writes to the same store.

* Names that match built-in JavaScript object properties, such as `constructor`, `toString`, or `__proto__`, now work like any other name. pnpm crashed, wrote a wrong lockfile, or silently skipped such names in:

  * `pnpm add`, `pnpm install`, and `pnpm import`, for dependencies, peer dependencies, and `file:` dependencies that point to a directory named `constructor`.
  * Catalog entries and catalog names. Pruning unused entries crashed, and a new catalog named `toString` was not written.
  * Workspace projects, project directories, and files inside injected packages.
  * Registry prefixes and override version references such as `$toString`.
  * Hoisting, `pnpm list`, and `pnpm why`.
  * Command names. `pnpm constructor` runs the `constructor` script like any other unknown command, and `pnpm help constructor` no longer crashes.
  * Resolving through a pnpr server when a project lives in a directory named `constructor`.

* `pnpm install` no longer re-resolves an up-to-date lockfile on every run when a patched package is a peer in a peer cycle [#16418](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16418).

* POSIX bin shims and the `pnpm`, `pn`, `pnpx`, and `pnx` launchers now run inside a Nix build, where the system default path holds none of the utilities they call. Installing again replaces the shims already in `node_modules` [#16377](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16377).

* In a project that pins another pnpm version, pnpm now passes a command with an option it does not know to the pinned version. Before, `pnpm install --auto-dedupe` failed with "Unknown option" even though the pinned pnpm supports it [#16353](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16353).

* pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_ALLOW_BUILDS` when `allowBuilds` is not an object or one of its values is not `true`, `false`, or a string. Such values used to be ignored silently.

* Removing a dependency whose bins are declared through `directories.bin` no longer leaves broken shims in `node_modules/.bin`.

* A custom resolver's `shouldRefreshResolution` hook that rejects no longer crashes pnpm with an unhandled rejection when another hook has already asked for a refresh.

#### Updating dependencies

* When `minimumReleaseAge` hides the version that `latest` points to, pnpm now falls back to a prerelease of the same major before a stable version of an older major. A stable version of the same major is still preferred. 
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(store): read msgpackr undefined in store index rows
prs.author: altaywtf
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm store prune` fails with `ERR_PNPM_STORE_DIR_PRUNE_STORE_INDEX` on a store where pnpm 11 installed a git-hosted dependency without a `package.json`. pnpm 11 packs `manifest: undefined` for that row, msgpackr writes `undefined` as fixext1 `d4 00 00`, and the records transcoder passed the ext through to `rmp_serde`, which `serde_json::Value` rejects.

- The transcoder now writes `nil` for msgpackr's `undefined`, so every reader (prefetch, prune, `find-hash`) reads the row with no manifest.
- Prune keeps a row it still cannot decode and reports the count. It used to abort after it had already deleted the CAS files, which left the index cleanup undone.

pnpm 11 is not affected: it decodes rows with msgpackr itself.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16421

## Squash Commit Body

```text
pnpm 11 packs `manifest: undefined` for a tarball without a
`package.json`, such as a git-hosted dependency, and msgpackr encodes
`undefined` as fixext1 `d4 00 00`. The records transcoder copied that
ext through, `rmp_serde` surfaced it as a newtype struct, and
`serde_json::Value` rejected it. Every reader treated the row as
undecodable, and `pnpm store prune` aborted on it after already
deleting unreferenced CAS files.

The transcoder now writes `nil` for msgpackr's `undefined`. Prune also
keeps any row it still cannot decode, since without its file list it
cannot tell whether the row references a removed file, and reports the
count instead of failing.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16421
```

prs.title: fix(lockfile): don't treat a patched peer collapsed by a peer cycle as stale
prs.author: lazerg
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16418.

When the resolver breaks a peer cycle, it writes the cyclic peer as a bare `name@version`, with no `(patch_hash=...)`. The check added in pnpm/pnpm#15336 expects every unmarked peer segment that names a patched registry package to carry the hash. So a lockfile with a patched peer in a cycle (`thread-loader@4.0.4(webpack@5.88.2)` with `webpack` patched) always read as stale. Every install re-resolved and wrote the same lockfile back.

The check now infers a missing hash only when the peer segment has its own suffix. A bare `name@version` peer is what the cycle collapse writes, so it is left alone. The marked-peer path and the dedupePeers case do not change. The fix is in both stacks.

Local check: I used a project with `webpack@5.88.2` (patched), `webpack-cli@5.1.4` and `thread-loader@4.0.4`, with `dedupePeers: false`. With 12.8.1, every `pnpm install --lockfile-only --trust-lockfile` runs `resolve_workspace`. With this branch, a repeat run skips it, and the lockfile stays byte-identical. pnpm 11.28.2 shows the same bug on the same project.

name@version, without its patch hash. checkPatchedDepPaths inferred a

prs.title: feat(pnpr): compute missing upstream tarball integrity
prs.author: krosci
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpr now computes a SHA-512 integrity for upstream package versions whose packuments omit `dist.integrity` (or carry an SRI with no hashes). When pnpr fetches a packument from a caching upstream, it downloads up to 64 such tarballs, caches them, and persists the normalized packument, so resolution and later tarball requests see the same integrity. A declared legacy `dist.shasum` is verified before its version is pinned.

Pinning is per version and never fails the packument. A version whose tarball is gone, whose bytes contradict its `shasum`, or whose dist is malformed keeps the metadata the upstream published, and the tarball route still refuses it. Reads of the cached packument do not retry those versions; the next refresh does. The downloads run without the package lock, which is striped and shared with hosted publishes. Under that lock, pnpr persists the pins before it promotes their tarballs into the cache. Cache-disabled upstreams serve the packument unchanged, because pnpr has nowhere to persist a computed pin. Malformed integrity values are still rejected by the tarball route.

Related to [pnpm/tasks#24](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/24).

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Upstream packuments may omit dist.integrity, leaving pnpm clients unable to
install those versions through pnpr.

When pnpr fetches a packument from a caching upstream, it downloads each
version that lacks a usable integrity (capped at 64 per fetch), verifies a
declared legacy shasum
…(truncated)

fix(store)!: coordinate concurrent read-only index access
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix `ReadOnlyStoreIndex` reporting "database disk image is malformed" or returning stale entries while another job writes to the same local store. It now participates in SQLite WAL locking and observes committed writes. Frozen-store callers explicitly use `ImmutableStoreIndex`.

This intentionally changes the exported reader's default. The maintainer requested a **major release of `@pnpm/store.index`** so existing FusePM reader code gets the fix by upgrading the package. External callers using the old reader for finalized stores on read-only filesystems must switch to `ImmutableStoreIndex`. The pnpm CLI and its internal consumers receive patch releases because their frozen-store behavior is preserved.

Reproduced the exact error locally with an immutable reader and a separate writer process. The database itself still passed SQLite's integrity check. The fixed `ReadOnlyStoreIndex` successfully reads the new entries.

Rust already distinguishes read-only and immutable access, so it needs no production change. Added coverage for WAL commits and checkpointed growth, and clarified that ordinary parallel installs and `--frozen-lockfile` allow shared-store writes; only `frozenStore` requires immutability.

CI exposed two test issues, also corrected here: a redundant overlap-marker assertion racing with holder release, and proxy TLS tests relying on an external endpoint that dropped the handshake. The latter now use a local HTTPS server with existing test certificates.

prs.title: fix(package-manager): accept injected optional peers in frozen installs
prs.author: tunglambk
prs.body:
## Summary

A fresh lockfile generated for an injected workspace package can record a sibling-supplied optional peer under the package snapshot's `optionalDependencies`. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` currently rejects that lockfile as outdated. Closes pnpm/pnpm#16428.

The directory-dependency freshness check now accepts a resolved optional peer in that snapshot group. It also recognizes the implicit `*` peer range generated when the optional peer is declared only in `peerDependenciesMeta`. Regression tests cover both manifest forms and verify that changing the optional flag still makes the lockfile stale.

Both cases work with pnpm v11.28.2, so this fix is limited to the affected v12 implementation.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
A fresh lockfile can place an injected package's resolved optional peer in its snapshot's optionalDependencies. The local directory freshness check treated that peer as an undeclared optional dependency. For metadata-only optional peers, it also compared the generated wildcard peer range against an empty peerDependencies map.

Accept snapshot optional dependency keys declared as optional peers and include their implicit wildcard ranges when checking package metadata. Keep rejecting a lockfile when the manifest's optional peer flag changes.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16428.
```

prs.title: docs: describe the mature fallback of time-based resolution
chore(release): 11.28.3
fix: hold a range pin's recorded pnpm to minimumReleaseAge
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16431.

A `devEngines.packageManager` range recorded the running pnpm in `packageManagerDependencies` without checking it against the project's `minimumReleaseAge`. The running pnpm is installed outside the project, so one contributor with a fresh global pnpm could write a version that everyone else's switch then refused with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION`.

Both stacks:

- When the running pnpm is about to be recorded for a range pin, pnpm checks it against the project's cutoff. The exemption the running version gets in self-update and the switch does not apply here. An immature running pnpm gives way to the newest version in the range that passes both `minimumReleaseAge` and the configured `trustPolicy`. If nothing in the range passes, the running version is kept. If the lookup itself fails (offline, registry error), pnpm warns and records nothing, and the next command retries. The command that records it keeps running on the current pnpm. Exact pins and `--frozen-lockfile` skip the lookup.

pnpm v12 only:

- The sync compared the lockfile against the running version, so a recorded version that still satisfied the range was overwritten whenever the running pnpm differed (the issue's 12.7.0 → 12.8.1 rewrite). It now keeps the locked version, as v11 already does, and only rewrites the specifier when the range changed.

Docs for `devEngines.packageManager` now say which version gets recorded first.

prs.title: refactor(ts): meet size and shape limits in 10 packages
docs(cli): correct the --force help text of install and add
fix(install): deduplicate onto a downgraded version with autoDedupe
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With `autoDedupe` enabled, downgrading a dependency in one workspace project left the other projects on the old version. A later `pnpm dedupe` then still found something to change. Closes pnpm/pnpm#16432.

Three separate causes, each covered by a test that fails without its fix:

- **Candidate weights.** When a resolution pass found duplicate versions, `prefer_candidate` gave each candidate the lockfile weight and **replaced** any weaker preference. The exact version a manifest names (`0.7.1` in the issue) lost its direct-dependency weight. It then tied with the version already in the lockfile (`0.7.2`), and the tie went to the highest version. The lockfile seed in `pnpm-lockfile-preferred-versions` **adds** the two weights, which is why `pnpm dedupe` got it right. `prefer_candidate` now uses the same helper (`add_weight_to_version_selector`, made public).
- **Store peek.** The npm resolver's store peek reused an edge's locked version whenever it still satisfied the range and the store had its manifest. Only an update or a `minimumReleaseAge` cutoff skipped it, so with `minimumReleaseAge: 0` deduplication never reached the picker. The walk now sets `repick_current_version` on an edge whose locked version it reopened. The store peek skips such an edge unless its spec is an exact version. Offline, when the picker finds no metadata (`ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_META`), the resolver still falls back to the locked manifest in the store, so an offline install keeps working.

prs.title: fix(dedupe): keep a hoisted optional peer's subtree on install's versions
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16447.

`pnpm dedupe --check` failed right after a fresh `pnpm install` when a project's optional peer is satisfied by a package another workspace project installs, and that package has a `*` dependency with several locked versions.

In the issue's repro, the root's `vitest` has an optional peer on `msw`, which only `packages/a` installs. After the importers' initial walks, the root hoists `msw@2.15.0` as a direct dependency. That occurrence (depth 0, importer order 0) wins ownership of the subtree's children. Whether it re-walks them depends on whether its context matches the one `packages/a` recorded:

- Fresh install: neither walk has a prior-lockfile key, so the contexts match. The root reads a's recording, and `@types/set-cookie-parser`'s `@types/node: *` stays on `22.20.4`, which a's direct-dependency preference picked.
- `pnpm dedupe` (`UpdateReuseScope::None`): a's walk carries prior-lockfile keys and the hoisted walk has none, so the contexts differ. The root re-walks, and its `*` pick sees only the equal-weight locked versions, so it takes the highest, `26.6.3`.

Under an update that unpins every edge (no selector, unlimited depth), the prior key pins nothing, so the recorded children context now leaves it out. Dedupe then reuses the recording just as install does. Updates with selectors or a `--depth` limit still compare the key, because there it can pin children.

The v11 CLI (11.28.3) passes `pnpm dedupe --check` on the same repro, so
…(truncated)

prs.title: refactor(ts): meet size and shape limits in 5 packages
fix(deps-resolver): drop a stale locked optional-peer version
prs.author: altaywtf
prs.body:
## Summary

After a provider bumps its exact dependency (`vue` 3.5.40 → 3.5.43), pnpm v12 kept an optional peer (`@vue/server-renderer` under `@vue/test-utils`) on the old locked version, so `install` and `dedupe` left two copies in the lockfile. The optional-peer hoist preferred any version the wanted lockfile pinned while it was still a candidate, and lockfile seeding keeps every locked version a candidate. A locked version now wins only while this run's reachable tree still resolves it. Otherwise the picker tries, in order, the locked versions this run resolved, every version this run resolved, and the locked versions, before any other candidate. prs.title: fix(gvs): run entry points loaded by CommonJS require hooks
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes `ts-node index.ts` (and any entry point that only a CommonJS `require.extensions` hook can load) failing with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` when the global virtual store injects its ESM `NODE_PATH` loader flag.

The cause is not the `module.register()` fallback. **Any** `--import` in `NODE_OPTIONS`, even an empty `--import=data:text/javascript,`, makes Node.js run the main entry point through the ESM loader. That happens on every version I tried: 18.20, 20.20, 22.14, 22.15, 24.11, 26. Node.js 24+ only looked unaffected in the issue because it strips TypeScript types natively. A fake `.custom` extension registered via `require.extensions` still fails there. So gating the flag on `module.registerHooks()` would not have fixed it.

The resolve hook now gives an entry point (`parentURL === undefined`, `file:` URL) that the ESM resolver could not classify (`format == null`) the `commonjs` format. That hands it back to the CommonJS loader, as Node.js does without `--import`. Entry points ending in `.js` or with no extension are excluded: Node.js may detect module syntax in them, and forcing `commonjs` breaks ESM-syntax `.js` files outside a `type: module` package (verified).

Why the fix is resolve-only rather than a `load` hook: on Node.js 22.15, registering any synchronous `load` hook, even a pass-through one, makes CommonJS mains run with `require.extensions` undefined.

## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16457.

A workspace project that declares `dependenciesMeta` and whose dependencies all resolve to workspace links never gets that `dependenciesMeta` recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml`, so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejects the lockfile the install just wrote. Nothing has to change for it to fail; a lockfile written a second ago is reported as out of date:

```text
$ pnpm install --lockfile-only
$ pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
[ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE] Cannot install with "frozen-lockfile" because pnpm-lock.yaml is not up to date with <ROOT>/packages/a/package.json

  Failure reason:
  importer dependencies meta (undefined) doesn't match package manifest dependencies meta ({"b":{"injected":true}})
```

`writeDirectDependencyRefs` in `pnpm11/installing/deps-resolver/src/updateLockfileImporters.ts` copies the manifest's `dependenciesMeta` onto the importer inside the loop over `dependenciesByProjectId[project.id]`. A project whose dependencies all resolved to workspace links has no entries in that map, so the copy never runs and the field stays out of the lockfile. `satisfiesPackageManifest` compares the manifest against the lockfile unconditionally, so the same install then fails its own up-to-date check. CI is the worst case, because `--frozen-lockfile` is the default there.

The fix hoists the copy above that loop, next to the other per-project lockfile writes.

prs.title: fix(cli): accept -s before an implicit script name
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm -s <script>` failed in pnpm v12 with "unexpected argument '-s' found". The universal-shorthand pass correctly leaves `-s` alone for the `pnpm <script>` fallback (it resolves to `run`, where `-s` is `--sequential`). But flag relocation only moves pre-subcommand tokens after a real subcommand, so `-s` stayed at the top level, where nothing declared it.

This adds a hidden top-level `-s` / `--sequential`, following the existing top-level `--if-present`. It is accepted only for `run` and the script fallback, and it is merged into the run arguments. pnpm v11 already accepts `pnpm -s lint` (it parses the fallback with `run`'s shorthands), so this is a v12-only fix.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#16446

fallback. Flag relocation only moves a pre-subcommand token after a real

- A config dependency installed online, then its project links and GVS links removed, then reinstalled with `--offline` from the store.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`@pnpm/napi` 12.8.0 started treating an embedder's `readPackageHook` as an untracked hook. This came with the global-pnpmfile fix in pnpm/pnpm#15187: the engine can't fingerprint a JS callback, so it records `untrackedPnpmfileReadPackageHook: true`. For Bit, which always passes a hook, every install that changes anything then skips the fast lockfile update and withholds the reuse seed. As a result, every dependency is resolved again.

This adds a `readPackageHookChecksum` install option. When it's set, the hooks are wrapped in `ChecksummedHooks`, which records the checksum as `pnpmfileChecksum` and marks the hook as tracked. The lockfile is then reused until the checksum changes, the same way it is for an edited `.pnpmfile.cjs`. This mirrors v11's programmatic `hooks.calculatePnpmfileChecksum`, so v11 needs no change.

The repeat-install shortcut detects a changed pnpmfile by its mtime, and an in-memory hook has none. Once the shortcut has accepted an install, it now also compares the embedder hook with what the lockfile records: the checksum, and whether an untracked `readPackage` hook appeared or went away. Without that, a changed checksum with unchanged manifests was reported as "Already up to date". The comparison runs after the shortcut's own checks, so an install the shortcut rejects never inspects the hooks.

Bit counterpart: teambit/bit#10748, which passes a checksum of its dependency-manifest transform.

feat: per-registry networkConcurrency in the registries setting
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A `registries` entry can now set `networkConcurrency`, the most requests pnpm keeps in flight to that registry's host:

```yaml
registries:
  https://npm.corp.example.com/:
    scopes: ["@acme"]
    networkConcurrency: 4
```

This builds on the per-origin timeout gate from pnpm/pnpm#15880. The use case is a rate-limited or fragile private registry, which can now be capped without lowering concurrency for npmjs.org and every other host.

Behavior:

- The cap applies to requests whose URL is on the entry's origin, including tarballs served from the same host. Requests to that origin still count against the overall `networkConcurrency`.
- Entries that share an origin share the smallest cap.
- A fetch timeout with active peers can still lower the origin to one request.
- The cap is keyed by the target origin, not the proxy, because it is about the registry server.
- An entry may set only `networkConcurrency`, for example for the default registry. Such an entry does not trigger the "matches no configured registry" warning, which reads only the server-description fields.
- Cargo and PyPI entries may set it too.
- It is read from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and the global `config.yaml`, since it does not affect the lockfile.
- `pnpm config get registries` shows it.
- Registry declarations sent to a pnpr server omit it. The server does not make the client's requests, and an older server would refuse an unknown field.

This is a new feature, so it is implemented only in pnpm v12
